title: Hold each 3 g hearing aid while the other hand swings its battery door open, then lay both in the drying case overnight
instruction: Open the battery door on each hearing aid, then lay both aids in the drying case for the night, doors open.
context: Hearing-aid users put their aids in a drying case every night, and the makers' instructions say to open each battery door first, so the zinc-air cell stops draining and moisture can get out. The aid weighs 3 g and its door is a 10 mm flap that clicks shut: pulled by its nail lip, an aid that nothing holds just slides or turns, so one hand holds the aid while the other swings the door open past its click.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. Two identical behind-the-ear hearing aids lie on their sides with their battery doors shut: each a beige plastic shell 4.0 cm long, 1.2 cm from back to front and 0.9 cm thick (3 g with its cell), a clear grey ear hook (3.6 mm tube) curving about 1.6 cm off its top end and a dark grey logo dot on each side near the top. The battery door is the shell's bottom 1.0 cm, hinged on a pin across the shell at the bottom end's front corner; a nail lip (1.5 mm thick, 7 mm tall, standing 8 mm out) stands on the bottom end at the back. The door clicks shut within 12 deg of shut, otherwise stays where it is put, and opens to 105 deg; a size 13 cell sits in it. Each aid lies with its bottom end toward the robot's right (-y), its back away from the robot and its hook curving toward the robot: one with its bottom end's centre at (36, 3), the other at (24, 3). Drying case: a white plastic box 10.4 (x) x 8.5 (y) x 2.2 cm, 300 g, centred at (30, 15.5), its lid (smoked grey) hinged along the back top edge and standing open at 100 deg; its top holds an open tray 9.2 (x) x 7.4 (y) cm and 8 mm deep with a grey floor, centred in the box. Both arms start at the ready pose with open grippers. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: A door is open at 60 deg or more. An aid lies in the case when its centre (2 cm up the shell from the bottom end) is at least 4 mm inside the tray's walls, it rests on the tray's floor (its centre at most 3 mm above lying flat) and it is within 20 deg of lying on its side. 1.0 (success): both aids in the case with their doors open, every finger pad of both grippers at least 2 cm from both aids, and nothing moving more than 2 mm over the last second, together for 1 s; this ends the trial. Otherwise, at the end of the run, for each aid: 0.25 if its door is open, and 0.25 more if it also lies in the case; at most 0.75. An aid laid in the case with its door shut scores nothing.
reset_notes: Close both battery doors (click them shut) and lay the aids back on their marks; stand the case on its marks with its lid open against its stop.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. Each aid is a free two-part articulation: shell (convex pieces, hook as capsules) and battery door on a hinge. The door's click is a spring pulling it shut within 12 deg (about 0.5 N at the lip); beyond that it stays put, like a real door pin's friction. The nail lip stands 8 mm out so the 15 mm-wide fingertips can take it; real lips stand 1-2 mm out and are opened with a fingernail. Case rigid, lid fixed open; cell not modelled.
